verses.original: Πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἐξουσίαις ὑπερεχούσαις ὑποτασσέσθω οὐ γὰρ ἔστιν ἐξουσία εἰ μὴ ὑπὸ Θεοῦ αἱ δὲ οὖσαι ὑπὸ Θεοῦ τεταγμέναι εἰσίν
verses.transliteration: Pasa psychē exousiais hyperechousais hypotassesthō ou gar estin exousia ei mē hypo Theou hai de ousai hypo Theou tetagmenai eisin
verses.literal: Everyone . . . must submit himself to the governing authorities . . . for there is no authority except . . . that which is from God The authorities that exist . . . have been appointed by God
verses.literalPt: TODA a alma esteja sujeita às potestades superiores; porque não há potestade que não venha de Deus; e as potestades que há foram ordenadas por Deus.

verses.original: ὥστε ὁ ἀντιτασσόμενος τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ διαταγῇ ἀνθέστηκεν οἱ δὲ ἀνθεστηκότες ἑαυτοῖς κρίμα λήμψονται
verses.transliteration: hōste ho antitassomenos tē exousia tē tou Theou diatagē anthestēken hoi de anthestēkotes heautois krima lēmpsontai
verses.literal: Consequently whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves
verses.literalPt: Por isso quem resiste à potestade resiste à ordenação de Deus; e os que resistem trarão sobre si mesmos a condenação.

verses.original: οἱ γὰρ ἄρχοντες οὐκ εἰσὶν φόβος τῷ ἀγαθῷ ἔργῳ ἀλλὰ τῷ κακῷ θέλεις δὲ μὴ φοβεῖσθαι τὴν ἐξουσίαν τὸ ἀγαθὸν ποίει καὶ ἕξεις ἔπαινον ἐξ αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: hoi gar archontes ouk eisin phobos tō agathō ergō alla tō kakō theleis de mē phobeisthai tēn exousian to agathon poiei kai hexeis epainon ex autēs
verses.literal: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct but to bad Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority Then do what is right and you will have his approval
verses.literalPt: Porque os magistrados não são terror para as boas obras, mas para as más. Queres tu, pois, não temer a potestade? Faze o bem, e terás louvor dela.

verses.original: Θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν σοὶ εἰς τὸ ἀγαθόν ἐὰν δὲ τὸ κακὸν ποιῇς φοβοῦ οὐ γὰρ εἰκῇ τὴν μάχαιραν φορεῖ Θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν ἔκδικος εἰς ὀργὴν τῷ τὸ κακὸν πράσσοντι
verses.transliteration: Theou gar diakonos estin soi eis to agathon ean de to kakon poiēs phobou ou gar eikē tēn machairan phorei Theou gar diakonos estin ekdikos eis orgēn tō to kakon prassonti
verses.literal: For he is God’s servant for your good But if you do wrong be afraid for he does not carry the sword in vain He is God’s servant an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer
verses.literalPt: Porque ela é ministro de Deus para teu bem. Mas, se fizeres o mal, teme, pois não traz debalde a espada; porque é ministro de Deus, e vingador para castigar o que faz o mal.

verses.original: Διὸ ἀνάγκη ὑποτάσσεσθαι οὐ μόνον διὰ τὴν ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν
verses.transliteration: Dio anankē hypotassesthai ou monon dia tēn orgēn alla kai dia tēn syneidēsin
verses.literal: Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority not only to avoid punishment but also as a matter of conscience
verses.literalPt: Portanto é necessário que lhe estejais sujeitos, não somente pelo castigo, mas também pela consciência.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ φόρους τελεῖτε λειτουργοὶ γὰρ Θεοῦ εἰσιν εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο προσκαρτεροῦντες
verses.transliteration: dia touto gar kai phorous teleite leitourgoi gar Theou eisin eis auto touto proskarterountes
verses.literal: This is also why . . . . . . you pay taxes For the authorities are God’s servants who devote themselves to their work
verses.literalPt: Por esta razão também pagais tributos, porque são ministros de Deus, atendendo sempre a isto mesmo.

verses.original: ἀπόδοτε πᾶσιν τὰς ὀφειλάς τῷ τὸν φόρον τὸν φόρον τῷ τὸ τέλος τὸ τέλος τῷ τὸν φόβον τὸν φόβον τῷ τὴν τιμὴν τὴν τιμήν
verses.transliteration: apodote pasin tas opheilas tō ton phoron ton phoron tō to telos to telos tō ton phobon ton phobon tō tēn timēn tēn timēn
verses.literal: Pay everyone what you owe him taxes to whom taxes are due revenue to whom revenue is due respect to whom respect is due honor to whom honor is due
verses.literalPt: Portanto, dai a cada um o que deveis: a quem tributo, tributo; a quem imposto, imposto; a quem temor, temor; a quem honra, honra.

verses.original: Μηδενὶ μηδὲν ὀφείλετε εἰ μὴ τὸ ἀλλήλους ἀγαπᾶν ὁ γὰρ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἕτερον νόμον πεπλήρωκεν
verses.transliteration: Mēdeni mēden opheilete ei mē to allēlous agapan ho gar agapōn ton heteron nomon peplērōken
verses.literal: Be indebted to no one . . . except . . . to one another in love For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law
verses.literalPt: A ninguém devais coisa alguma, a não ser o amor com que vos ameis uns aos outros; porque quem ama aos outros cumpriu a lei.

verses.original: τὸ γάρ Οὐ μοιχεύσεις Οὐ φονεύσεις Οὐ κλέψεις Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις καὶ εἴ τις ἑτέρα ἐντολή ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ ἀνακεφαλαιοῦται ἐν τῷ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν
verses.transliteration: to gar Ou moicheuseis Ou phoneuseis Ou klepseis Ouk epithymēseis kai ei tis hetera entolē en tō logō toutō anakephalaioutai en tō Agapēseis ton plēsion sou hōs seauton
verses.literal: The commandments Do not commit adultery Do not murder Do not steal Do not covet and any other commandments are summed up in this one decree - Love your neighbor as yourself
verses.literalPt: Com efeito: Não adulterarás, não matarás, não furtarás, não darás falso testemunho, não cobiçarás; e se há algum outro mandamento, tudo nesta palavra se resume: Amarás ao teu próximo como a ti mesmo.

verses.original: ἡ ἀγάπη τῷ πλησίον κακὸν οὐκ ἐργάζεται πλήρωμα οὖν νόμου ἡ ἀγάπη
verses.transliteration: hē agapē tō plēsion kakon ouk ergazetai plērōma oun nomou hē agapē
verses.literal: Love does no wrong to its neighbor Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law
verses.literalPt: O amor não faz mal ao próximo. De sorte que o cumprimento da lei é o amor.

verses.original: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰδότες τὸν καιρόν ὅτι ὥρα ἤδη ὑμᾶς ἐξ ὕπνου ἐγερθῆναι νῦν γὰρ ἐγγύτερον ἡμῶν ἡ σωτηρία ἢ ὅτε ἐπιστεύσαμεν
verses.transliteration: Kai touto eidotes ton kairon hoti hōra ēdē hymas ex hypnou egerthēnai nyn gar engyteron hēmōn hē sōtēria ē hote episteusamen
verses.literal: And do this understanding the occasion The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed
verses.literalPt: E isto digo, conhecendo o tempo, que já é hora de despertarmos do sono; porque a nossa salvação está agora mais perto de nós do que quando aceitamos a fé.

verses.original: ἡ νὺξ προέκοψεν ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤγγικεν ἀποθώμεθα οὖν τὰ ἔργα τοῦ σκότους ἐνδυσώμεθα δὲ τὰ ὅπλα τοῦ φωτός
verses.transliteration: hē nyx proekopsen hē de hēmera ēngiken apothōmetha oun ta erga tou skotous endysōmetha de ta hopla tou phōtos
verses.literal: The night is nearly over the day has drawn near So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light
verses.literalPt: A noite é passada, e o dia é chegado. Rejeitemos, pois, as obras das trevas, e vistamo-nos das armas da luz.

verses.original: ὡς ἐν ἡμέρᾳ εὐσχημόνως περιπατήσωμεν μὴ κώμοις καὶ μέθαις μὴ κοίταις καὶ ἀσελγείαις μὴ ἔριδι καὶ ζήλῳ
verses.transliteration: hōs en hēmera euschēmonōs peripatēsōmen mē kōmois kai methais mē koitais kai aselgeiais mē eridi kai zēlō
verses.literal: Let us behave decently as in the daytime not in carousing and drunkenness not in sexual immorality and debauchery not in dissension and jealousy
verses.literalPt: Andemos honestamente, como de dia; não em glutonarias, nem em bebedeiras, nem em desonestidades, nem em dissoluções, nem em contendas e inveja.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἐνδύσασθε τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν καὶ τῆς σαρκὸς πρόνοιαν μὴ ποιεῖσθε εἰς ἐπιθυμίας
verses.transliteration: alla endysasthe ton Kyrion Iēsoun Christon kai tēs sarkos pronoian mē poieisthe eis epithymias
verses.literal: Instead clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ and make no provision for the desires of the flesh
verses.literalPt: Mas revesti-vos do Senhor Jesus Cristo, e não tenhais cuidado da carne em suas concupiscências.
